Article id: configure-roles-and-permissions
Article: Assign user roles and configure permission levels
Protect sensitive clinical and financial data by tailoring access for your staff. Only practice managers and primary administrators can modify security credentials.

1. Go to **Settings > Practice Staff > Roles & Permissions**.
2. Click **Create New Role** or select an existing title from the directory.
3. Toggle permissions across categories, including *Billing*, *Patient Charts*, and *System Settings*.
4. Click **Assign Users**, select the staff members who require this profile, and click **Save Changes**.

**Limits & Conditions:** Every active user profile must be assigned to at least one role. Direct permission overrides on individual accounts are not permitted; all restrictions must flow through the assigned role.

**Troubleshooting:** If a staff member cannot view a restricted menu after saving, verify their account status is active and have them clear their browser cache before logging back in.

Ticket:
Question regarding user role adjustments and permissions audit

Hello support team, I am terribly sorry to bother you with this administrative task, but we are currently reviewing our internal security setup across our large provider network. I need to restrict access to certain sensitive financial ledgers and make sure our billing staff only see what is necessary. Could someone please guide me through auditing our custom permission levels and updating the user roles accordingly? Thank you so much for your time and assistance.

Auto-reply:
To audit and adjust permissions, go to **Settings > Practice Staff > Roles & Permissions**. Select the role used by your billing staff (or create a new role with **Create New Role**). Use the toggles to enable only the necessary **Billing** permissions and disable any financial ledger access. After adjusting, click **Assign Users**, ensure the correct staff are linked to the role, and press **Save Changes**. Verify each user’s account is active; if a menu still doesn’t appear, have the user clear their browser cache and log in again.
